test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
A sentence is provided in direct speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding indirect speech.

Tom said, "I have been working all day."

options.text: Tom said he had worked all day.
Tom said he had been working all day.
Tom said he has been working all day.
Tom said he was working all day.

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Tom said he had been working all day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **direct speech**, where Tom says, "I have been working all day."
 
• In **indirect speech**, the present perfect continuous tense ("have been working") changes to the **past perfect continuous tense** ("had been working") because the reporting verb "said" is in the past tense.
 
• The correct option must reflect this tense shift, while maintaining the meaning of the sentence.

Correct sentence: *Tom said he had been working all day.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Explanation of incorrect options:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** "Tom said he had worked all day." 
 - This is incorrect because it changes the tense to past perfect ("had worked") but does not reflect the continuous nature of the original statement.
 
• **Option 3:** "Tom said he has been working all day." 
 - This is incorrect because the present perfect continuous tense ("has been working") is not appropriate in indirect speech when the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
• **Option 4:** "Tom said he was working all day." 
 - This is incorrect because the past continuous tense ("was working") does not accurately convey the sense of completion and duration implied by the original present perfect continuous tense.
